newsitem.title: USA: Bank of N.Y. exec sees strong '97 for munis.
newsitem.headline: Bank of N.Y. exec sees strong '97 for munis.

text.p: James Cooner, senior vice president of Bank of New York Co's tax-exempt bond department, said Monday he expects a rebound for the municipal bond market in 1997.
"After a stay in the doldrums that lasted several years, municipal bonds will rebound with a vengeance in 1997," Cooner said in an analysis of market prospects for next year.
Cooner noted that voters approved $10 billion, or 70 percent, of the bonds on the Nov 5 ballot, the second largest amount ever approved in a single day.

He said that positive endorsement for munis helped counter recent negative news from such developments as declining new issue supply, possible tax law changes, and Orange County, Calif.'s 1994 bankruptcy.
Cooner estimated that 1997 volume would soar to $200 billion, from about $165 billion this year.
He said credit quality is on the rise, but warned that the outlook for electric utilities and hospital bonds was uncertain because of utility deregulation and health care reform.
